question.ask: How many tasks are waiting on a client?

text.text: For one freelancer and their clients. One row per client. Open a client to see their tasks, files and updates together. Tick Visible to client on a task to show it on their page.
This is what a client sees. Share only this page, never the admin home. Copy it for each client and change the filters.
Questions? Reply to the latest update or email the studio.
Add the client as a row and set the status to Onboarding.
Copy the sample portal page and rename it.
Filter every list so it shows only that client.
Tick Visible to client on the tasks you want them to see.
Share the page link, not the admin home.
Keep internal tasks unticked. They stay hidden from the portal.

Only the tasks ticked Visible to client, the files marked approved, and the updates you post. They never see the admin home or the other clients. Check the portal page signed out before you send the link.
Post one short update a week even when nothing changed; silence is what makes clients nervous.
Move a task to Waiting on client the moment you need something, so the dashboard shows it.
An approval is a record that someone said yes. Capture it in the file row so that nobody has to search email later.
Next task moved to In progress
If the client does not answer
Day 3: a one-line reminder with the link.
Day 7: a call or message, and a note in the update log.
Move the dependent task to Waiting on client so the schedule is honest.
